title: Elysium Analytics - Renewal, Scaling, and KMS Ops Sync
summary: Check-in to align on renewal timing (Feb 2027), proposed capacity uplift for EU region, KMS/HSM integration questions, and a short pilot to validate latency under workload. Agreement to provide updated pricing and pilot runbook.
topics: current usage and spinning pattern (peak token rates and KV cache hit rates)
EU region private deployment vs Redwood Dedicated
KMS/HSM integration and audit log requirements
contract extension term and staged capacity ramp
action_items: Ethan Cole | Share updated quote with EU regional pricing and term options | 2026-12-13
Samir Patel | Draft pilot runbook + benchmark plan (latency/throughput) and share infra reqs | 2026-12-16
Leila Soto | Provide current onprem network egress/cost numbers and KMS contact | 2026-12-15
Marco Ruiz | Send SOC2/ISO audit checklist items they need for legal review | 2026-12-14
next_steps: Redwood to send updated proposal and per-region cost delta by Mon 12/13
Schedule a 2-week pilot starting late Jan to validate EU latency with 10% traffic mirroring
Customer to share KMS endpoints + contact for integration planning
Follow-up call week of 12/20 to confirm pilot dates and PO timing
header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood CSM); Priya Raman (Elysium Head of ML), Jonas Berg (Elysium VP Eng), Leila Soto (Elysium Cloud Infra), Marco Ruiz (Elysium Security)
transcript: [00:00] Ethan Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for blocking time. quick check-in today, we wanted to run through the renewal timeline and the EU scaling ask that you flagged last week.
[00:18] Priya Raman: Yeah thanks Ethan. we've got a few minutes to cover the high level. main concern is latency for EU customers and then the KMS integration for some PHI-adjacent logs.

[00:30] Jonas Berg: Right, and also we need clarity on how Redwood Dedicated vs Private would affect throughput and the unit pricing — like what's the tradeoff if we go private in eu-west-1 vs just using Dedicated capacity.

[00:45] Samir Patel: Sure, I can jump in there — fundamentally Dedicated gives you predictable throughput with reserved cards, private (VPC) gives you more control over networking and KMS/HSM but there's more setup effort and slightly different SLA cadence. in practice the perf is similar but egress and ops differ.
[01:10] Leila Soto: When you say setup effort, what does that mean for our infra team? we've got strict key rotations and we need HSM-backed keys for a subset of requests.

[01:28] Samir Patel: Good q. For KMS/HSM we support bringing your own key through our KMS connector; if you want a dual-HSM handshake that's an extra ops step — we documented it but it does need a short on-prem agent or a private peering. We'll include that in the runbook.
[01:50] Priya Raman: Also curious about the KV cache behavior across regions — if we mirror traffic to EU, will the cache warm-up cause latency spikes in the pilot?

[02:05] Samir Patel: There can be a warm-up window. We recommend a prefix cache seeding strategy. for mirroring we'd do progressive ramp from 1% to 10% over 48 hours so the KV cash — sorry KV cache — warms without big spikes.
[02:25] Jonas Berg: And the SLA on tail latency? Our SLO is 200ms p95 for short completions, how close can Redwood get in the EU private setup?

[02:38] Maya Li: From our benchmarks, with dedicated RTX clusters and network peering we typically see 120–160ms p95 for sub-512 token contexts. we'll include model variant profiles. Samir, should we call out the sequence length assumptions?
[02:55] Samir Patel: Yes we'll surface the model + seq length. For Elysium's typical queries (avg 180 tokens) we can hit those numbers with the recommended batching config and prefix caching enabled.
[03:12] Priya Raman: Great. Pricing — we gave a rough SKU earlier; can you walk through the delta for adding EU dedicated nodes vs adding Private in a single AZ?

[03:25] Ethan Cole: Sure. Quick summary: Dedicated is reserved pools billed monthly; Private has a platform fee plus infra overlay for the VPC/onprem option. For EU we quote a ~12% uplift for Private because of HSM/KMS integrations and support SLA. we'll send a line-item doc.
[03:45] Marco Ruiz: For compliance, we'll need audit logs and immutable retention for 12 months. do you support that in the private plane — plane/pane — control plane?
[04:00] Maya Li: Yes, we have configurable audit log retention, and we can route logs to customer S3 or their SIEM. There is a retention add-on for long-term storage if you need >90 days.
[04:18] Marco Ruiz: Ok, and encryption at rest with HSM-backed keys is required for the subset of PHI. any gotchas?

[04:30] Samir Patel: Not many. the only thing is key rotation coordination — if you rotate keys frequently we'll need a maintenance window or a seamless key rollover plan to avoid token decryption failures. we have docs and a small automation script we can run with your team.
[04:50] Jonas Berg: On the timeline, we're aiming to have the contract in place by Feb 1 2027 to align with our fiscal cycle. can you accommodate that and the staged ramp over Q1?

[05:05] Ethan Cole: Yes that's doable. Typical path is sign amendment in Jan, run pilot in late Jan/early Feb, then staged activation in Mar-April. We'll align milestones to your retention and PO timing.
[05:20] Priya Raman: For the pilot specifics — what throughput will you test? our current peaks are ~3.2k tokens/sec across the cluster, with bursts to 6k during batch windows.

[05:36] Samir Patel: We'll mirror a subset of traffic at 10% which maps to about 320 tokens/sec baseline; for burst testing we can synthetic load to 6k to verify autoscale response and scheduler behavior. we'll record p50/p95/p99 and cost delta metrics.
[05:55] Leila Soto: Also need to confirm egress costs if we keep traffic in EU vs routing to US-hosted endpoints. we have budget constraints here.

[06:08] Ethan Cole: We'll include egress line items. For private in EU, egress is minimal if you keep assets in-region. For Dedicated hosted from Redwood US, egress hits your cloud provider rates. we'll show both options in the quote.

[06:25] Jonas Berg: Any competitors we should be aware of? BigCloudAI quoted a 'global edge' product but their audit trail was weak. ModelServeCo offered lower unit cost but had longer lead time for KMS.
[06:39] Priya Raman: We like Redwood's observability and rollouts — that's one reason we're pushing for an extension. but cost is a sticking point.
[06:50] Ethan Cole: Understood. we can propose a 12-month vs 24-month term with stepped discounts for committed usage. that usually helps balance cost and predictability.
[07:05] Maya Li: We can also propose a usage-smoothing credit for the first quarter of the ramp to ease the budget hit.
[07:18] Marco Ruiz: On legal, our procurement team will ask for SOC2 artifact and a data processing addendum. can you provide the doc set so our lawyers can pre-check it?
[07:32] Maya Li: Absolutely, we'll share SOC2 type II report, ISO attestation, and a standard DPA. Ethan will drop them in the binder.
[07:45] Priya Raman: Quick technical: what model variants will you recommend for our latency-sensitive flows? we use a mix: small summarization and longer generation for contextual answers.

[07:58] Samir Patel: For summarization pick the trimmed-quantized variant; for longer generation we recommend the high-memory variant in Dedicated to avoid kv-cache thrash. we'll put explicit model names in the runbook, though note sometimes transcription or model names get munged in docs — we'll be explicit.
[08:20] Jonas Berg: About failover, if the EU region loses capacity, can Redwood failover to US but keep data residency constraints? that's a concern for us.

[08:32] Ethan Cole: We have a policy-based fallback that can fail to a compatible variant in a different region, but for data residency we can restrict fallbacks for specific requests that contain PHI — those will error rather than failover unless you opt-in.
[08:50] Leila Soto: We'll likely mark PHI-tagged routes as no-failover. For others we can accept fallback to reduce downtime.

[09:02] Priya Raman: Ok. let's talk numbers for capacity uplift. current committed baseline is 2 reserved nodes. we're asking for plan for 8 nodes in EU so we can handle peak 6k token bursts. cost estimate?
[09:15] Ethan Cole: Rough math: 2 -> 8 nodes increases reserved fees by ~3.6x. we'll send exacts, but with a 24-month commitment we can discount per-node by ~18%.
[09:30] Jonas Berg: If we do that, what's the lead time to provision in EU private vs Dedicated?
[09:40] Samir Patel: Dedicated: 5–7 business days after PO. Private (VPC) with KMS: 2–3 weeks because of peering and HSM provisioning. onprem is longer depending on your hardware lane.
[09:58] Marco Ruiz: Any network requirements? our infra team needs a checklist.
[10:05] Samir Patel: We'll send a 1-page network checklist: CIDR blocks, peering ports, TLS cert thumbprints, and KMS endpoints. also recommended MTU and bandwidth floor for stable tail latency.
[10:20] Leila Soto: Please include expected egress metrics by traffic class. that'll help with budgeting.
[10:28] Ethan Cole: Will do. Samir will own the pilot runbook and bench plan.
[10:35] Priya Raman: One more ask: we'd like a canary rollout plan for the staged activation — we have teams that can't tolerate any user-facing degradations.
[10:47] Maya Li: We support canary rollouts and traffic splitting. we'll propose a 3-stage canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback triggers on latency or error rate thresholds.
[11:05] Jonas Berg: Do you have out-of-the-box metrics we can ingest? or do we need custom exporters?
[11:12] Samir Patel: We publish Prometheus metrics and a hosted dashboard. we can also forward traces to your Jaeger/Tempo if you prefer.
[11:24] Priya Raman: That works. Let's talk about the renewal terms briefly — extension plus additional committed nodes — are there minimums for the discount tiers?
[11:36] Ethan Cole: Discount tiers kick in at the 10-node commitment mark and annualized terms. if you prefer a blended approach we can craft a multi-year cadence with top-up options.
[11:50] Marco Ruiz: Legal will likely push for a termination clause if compliance fails. we should pre-discuss SLA credits and remediation windows.
[12:00] Maya Li: We can include SLA credits against monthly invoice for downtime beyond target. we'll note the remediation windows and escalation contacts.
[12:12] Priya Raman: Ok, anything we're missing on the technical side?
[12:18] Leila Soto: I wanted to flag that our internal firewall team may require specific IP allowlist changes; will you provide static egress IPs for private?
[12:28] Samir Patel: For private we can provide stable egress ranges. for Hosted Dedicated there are still stable ranges but fewer guarantees unless you opt into VPC peering.
[12:40] Jonas Berg: Let's recap so we have alignment on next steps before we run out of time.

[12:45] Ethan Cole: Recap: Redwood to send updated quote (EU region, Dedicated vs Private options, egress line items, 12/13). Samir to share pilot runbook and network checklist (12/16). Elysium to provide KMS contact and egress numbers (12/15). Marco to send audit items (12/14). Plan follow-up week of 12/20 to lock pilot dates.
[13:10] Priya Raman: Sounds good, thanks all. quick note, we'd prefer a 12- or 18-month term if it helps with budget, but we'll see the numbers.
[13:20] Ethan Cole: Understood. we'll include 12/18/24 month pricing scenarios. anything else?
[13:26] Marco Ruiz: No further items from security. we'll review the docs when you send them.
[13:32] Leila Soto: one last thing — can you include a short performance appendix with p95 numbers for the quantized variants? that will help our infra team make a call.
[13:42] Samir Patel: Yep we'll append the perf appendix. expect it with the quote.
[13:48] Ethan Cole: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing. Maya will send SOC2 and DPA as part of the package.
[13:55] Priya Raman: Thanks, talk soon.
[14:00] (meeting ends)
